newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria finds crude oil in border area near Benin.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria finds crude oil in border area near Benin.

text.p: Crude oil deposits have been discovered in south-western Tungbeji Island, a Nigerian border town near its western neighbour Benin, the military officer in charge of the area said on Friday.
The News Agency of Nigeria said Wing Commander Samuel Ewang announced the find when Works and Housing minister Major General AbdulKareem Adisa visited Ogun state.

"The discovery of the mineral resource has prompted Benin Republic to invite French experts to the island...they are luring Nigerians on the island to its side with a view to laying claim to the whole territory," Ewang said.
Nigeria and its eastern neighbour Cameroon are currently at odds over Bakassi peninsula in the oil-rich Gulf of Guinea which each side claims and where their forces have fought repeatedly.
Ewang did not say when production would begin in Tungbeji.
Nigeria, Africa's leading producer of oil, derives more than 90 percent of its foreign earnings from crude oil exports. Benin and Cameroon are much smaller producers.
